color.definition: A visual attribute of things that results from the light they emit or transmit or reflect.

viscosity.definition: Resistance of a liquid to shear forces (and hence to flow).

legs.definition: The streams of wine that run down a glass after it is swirled.

rim.definition: The upper edge of a wine glass that touches the mouth.

opacity.definition: The quality of being opaque to a degree.

hue.definition: The quality of a color as determined by its dominant wavelength.

depth.definition: The extent downward or backward or inward.

brilliance.definition: A light within the field of vision that is brighter than the brightness to which the eyes are adapted.

sediment.definition: Small solid particles that settle at the bottom of a liquid.

aroma.definition: Any property detected by the olfactory system.

nose.definition: The organ of smell and entrance to the respiratory tract.

floral.definition: Relating to or associated with flowers.

fruity.definition: Tasting or smelling richly of or as of fruit.

earthy.definition: Of or consisting of or resembling earth.

spicy.definition: Producing a burning sensation on the taste nerves.

herbaceous.definition: Characteristic of a nonwoody herb or plant part.

mineral.definition: A flavor or aroma in wine that suggests stone or chalk.

oaky.definition: Having an aroma or flavor associated with contact with oak wood during production or storage.
oaky.exampleUsage: The educational tasting chart uses 'oaky' to describe a wood-related aroma.

body.definition: The entire physical structure of an organism (an animal, plant, or human being).
body.exampleUsage: The body was identified during the lesson.

tannin.definition: Any of various complex phenolic substances of plant origin.

sweetness.definition: The property of tasting as if it contains sugar.

finish.definition: (wine tasting) the taste of a wine on the back of the tongue (as it is swallowed).

balance.definition: Harmonious arrangement or relation of parts or elements within a whole (as in a design).

complexity.definition: The quality of being intricate and compounded.

structure.definition: The manner of construction of something and the arrangement of its parts.

mouthfeel.definition: The measurable set of sensations a food or drink creates in the mouth as it is tasted is called mouthfeel. Trained panels assess these changing sensations with standardized scales.

length.definition: The linear extent in space from one end to the other.

dry.definition: Without a mucous or watery discharge.

sweet.definition: (used of wines) having a high residual sugar content.

crisp.definition: (of something seen or heard) clearly defined.

smooth.definition: (of a body of water) free from disturbance by heavy waves.

velvety.definition: Smooth and soft to sight or hearing or touch or taste.

bold.definition: Having a strong, intense flavor or character.

delicate.definition: Exquisitely fine and subtle and pleasing.

rich.definition: Having a full, concentrated flavor and texture.

light.definition: (used of color) having a relatively small amount of coloring agent.

full-bodied.definition: Describing a taste or flavor that is rich, powerful, rounded, and complex.

cheese-pairing.definition: The practice of selecting cheese and a beverage because their flavors are considered complementary.
cheese-pairing.exampleUsage: The museum exhibit explains cheese pairing as a flavor-matching concept.

meat-pairing.definition: The practice of matching meat dishes with a beverage based on flavor characteristics.
meat-pairing.exampleUsage: The course glossary defines meat pairing as a food-and-beverage matching concept.

seafood-pairing.definition: The practice of matching seafood dishes with a beverage based on flavor characteristics.
seafood-pairing.exampleUsage: The glossary uses seafood pairing as an example of flavor matching.

dessert-pairing.definition: The practice of matching desserts with a beverage based on sweetness, acidity, or other flavor characteristics.
dessert-pairing.exampleUsage: The educational chart labels dessert pairing as a flavor-matching category.

appetizer.definition: Food or drink to stimulate the appetite (usually served before a meal or as the first course).

main-course.definition: The principal dish in a formal meal is served as the meal’s main part, after the opening courses.

palate-cleanser.definition: A neutral food or drink used between different tastes to reduce lingering flavors in the mouth.
palate-cleanser.exampleUsage: Plain water can serve as a palate cleanser during a sensory exercise.

tasting-menu.definition: A set menu made up of several small courses chosen to present a sequence of flavors.
tasting-menu.exampleUsage: The culinary course discusses how a tasting menu is organized into small courses.

wine-flight.definition: A set of small wine samples presented together for comparison.
wine-flight.exampleUsage: The textbook defines a wine flight as several samples compared side by side.

cheese-board.definition: A serving board or platter arranged with different cheeses and often other foods.
cheese-board.exampleUsage: The cheese board contained several labeled varieties.
